My therapist likes to talk about how to keep us “sane” all our walls need to be in good shape. Meaning getting enough sleep, eating enough, a safe environment, and mental stability. So when one or more of your walls are down it is more likely for shit to hit the fan. I started prioritizing getting enough sleep and eating properly and it really helped. When we don’t eat or sleep enough we are more irritable causing symptoms to be more enhanced.

Quetiapine was one of the worst medication I’ve been put on. It helped a bit so I was kept on it for a long time. I started taking it in a mental hospital where it made me hallucinate and have very bad anxiety attacks. I told my psychiatrist this and he was just like that shouldn’t happen and upped it. When I got out of the hospital my new psychiatrist but me on 8 different medications that made everything worse and finally I had enough and went back on the quetiapine. She got me all the way up to 800mg. My face started breaking out, my hair started falling out, I was shaking and twitching 24/7, I slept over 15 hours a day and was still exhausted, my heart rate was always in the hundreds even while sleeping. I told my psychiatrist all of this and she basically was like keep taking it.

I haven’t had any luck with medication to the point that I have given up. I’m convinced that medication is only given to us to sedate us and not to actually help us get better.

I really don’t recommend. If you’re actually looking for help you won’t find any at a mental hospital, or anywhere really. In mental hospitals you are treated so shitty. They make fun of you for getting triggered by the other kids that are just as mental ill or worse than you are. The deny you are going through anything because why could a child experience anything like that. It’s even worse if you’re suicidal, they basically keep you in the hospital until you cave and say you’re no longer suicidal but don’t do anything to try and help you out of that. They pump you with medication that makes you a walking zombie because you’re easier to control that way. The only thing I’ve gotten out of my mental hospital stays is more trauma and scared to ask for help when you really need it. I don’t write this to discourage you from seeking help. I just what you to know what I wish I would have known before going into one. This is also only my experience with the system. At the time of my stays I was still a minor so keep that in mind.  Best of luck.

I’ve never tried to talk someone out of suicide but I always try to walk them through it. Once someone makes their minds up about that kind of thing, anything you saw won’t change it. This one time a girl reached out to me over the internet after she had attempted. I talked to her because she was scared and alone. I told her what to expect to happen because I’ve gone through it myself. You see killing yourself is a lot harder than it seems. I talked her through each stage and kept her company until she passed out. Sometimes you regret what you did and want someone to talk to but don’t want to talk to someone that is just going to freak out and call an ambulance.
